He asks why many young people do not know their own scriptures, and believes that capitalism has hollowed people out from within and pushed them towards an emotional intoxication. To Javed Akhtar's argument that religious consolation is false consolation, the writer replies that questioning whether a belief is true is not denying its human usefulness.

The conclusion is that religion needs not rejection but reform: reviving values such as compassion, duty and peace. According to the writer, defending religion means defending not its name but the humanity within it.
nazar: The most useful part of the essay is where it calls corridors and 'dharma-raksha' squads a corrupted form of religion; this criticism from within faith matters. But we disagree with the writer's claim that critics of religion are the ones who promote hypocritical gurus and frenzy. Turning the crowd into a weapon is the work of the politics of power, not of those who ask questions. Ambedkar's dharma of principles also rested on the test of equality, and that is the real condition of this debate.
sawal: Who sowed the acacia on the fallow land, outsiders or our own?
ref: Javed Akhtar
A lyricist and screenwriter, known for his open views in public debates on atheism and religion.
Dharmo rakshati rakshitah
A saying found in the Manusmriti, meaning that dharma protects the one who protects dharma.

h: An evening in Raipur: raga, a book release and poems
dek: On Hindwi Bela, Geetanjali Sinha writes about the discussion in Raipur on Anand Bahadur's new poetry collection 'Bahar Bhi Ek Bheetar Hai' and also puts a finger on the local politics of literature.
body: A three-and-a-half-hour event was held at Vimtara Bhawan in Raipur on Anand Bahadur's poetry collection 'Bahar Bhi Ek Bheetar Hai' (There Is an Inside Outside Too). The collection has come from Kalamshala Prakashan. Geetanjali Sinha learnt of it from an Instagram story by Kalamshala's editor and poet Ashutosh Prasiddh, and she came all the way from Fingeshwar in Gariaband district. Arriving late, she missed the first session.

It began with the 'Naad Brahma' session, in which young singer Vasu Gandharva sang a khayal and a thumri in raga Jog, with Ashok Kurmi on the tabla. After that the collection was released, followed by a discussion on it in the session called 'Baat Bolegi'.

Hindwi's editor Avinash Mishra called these poems weightless. Chief guest Keshav Tiwari said that everyday life comes into them with simple honesty. Novelist and critic Prabhu Narayan Verma praised Anand for staying away from literary manoeuvring and keeping busy with writing, translation and fiction. Presiding, Dinesh Kushwaha said these poems say extraordinary things in plain words.

Then 'Das Dwar' (Ten Doors), a collection of ten classic stories of the world translated by Anand Bahadur, was released, also from Kalamshala. The last session was poetry reading, with seven poets including Alim Naqvi, Piyush Kumar and Imran Abbas. Piyush Kumar's poem reminded the writer of the fields, flowers and Govardhan puja of her childhood.

The report ends with the writer's own view: to write one needs a personality that is not broken by criticism and not puffed up by praise. She questions local literary politics, which in her view is often in the hands of opportunists and keeps capable writers away from good debates.
nazar: Unlike the literature festivals of big cities, such evenings in places like Raipur are the real ground of Hindi: small publishers, local poets and a woman reader who came from a distant town. It is also worth noting that the news reached her through Instagram, and literature's new reach is being built through social media. One lack stands out: according to the report, all those who spoke and read on stage were men, which is an old disease of Hindi events.
sawal: Why did the news reach a small-town reader only through Instagram?
ref: Raga Jog
A raga of Hindustani music sung in the first watch of the night, in which both Gandhars are used.
